title: What the Quarry Fell On
description: The bottom of the goblin warren is gone. Something took it out, in courses, and put a staircase where it was.

the_floor_of_the_warren.title: Down what replaced the floor
the_floor_of_the_warren.objective: The warren floor did not fall in. Go down the spoil stair to see what took it out. It ends at the headings, where Coyle keeps the hut.
the_floor_of_the_warren.journal: For two years, Ilse has said something was taking the bottom of the warren, floor by floor. She was right about what was happening, but not the verb. Nothing is taking it. Someone is buying it out, one course at a time, and paying men to carry it away.

the_works.title: Walk the works
the_works.objective: Nobody has stopped you yet. Walk the works and count what you see. Then return to Coyle's hut and tell her the number.
the_works.journal: Sawn steps. A handrail. A bucket of sand on each landing for fires. Below, a plank floor the size of the market square, a bell, a board of numbered pegs, a canteen, and two hundred people working in shifts. None of it is hidden. It's simply eleven miles from anyone who would object.

walked_the_works.title: Two hundred people
walked_the_works.journal: I walked the whole works. A woman with a water clock stopped me politely to ask my peg number. Six faces are being cut at a costed rate toward one point beneath the old quarry. No one down there knows what's at the point, or has asked. They're paid by the day; down there, that's the only unit that matters.

turned_back.title: Back up the stair
turned_back.journal: I reached the muster floor, watched a bell ring and forty people change direction, then went back up the stair. I haven't told Ilse what lies under her warren. I'm not sure which part frightens me.
